from astropy.modeling import models as m
from astropy.modeling import separable
import numpy as np
cm = m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5)
left = m.Pix2Sky_TAN()
right = cm
noutp = separable._compute_n_outputs(left,right)
# compute cleft
if isinstance(left, separable.Model):
    cleft = separable._coord_matrix(left,'left', noutp)
else:
    cleft = np.zeros((noutp, left.shape[1]))
    cleft[: left.shape[0], : left.shape[1]] = left
# compute cright
if isinstance(right, separable.Model):
    cright = separable._coord_matrix(right,'right', noutp)
else:
    cright = np.zeros((noutp, right.shape[1]))
    cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = right
print('noutp', noutp)
print('cleft:\n', cleft)
print('cright:\n', cright)
print('separable._cstack(cleft,cright):\n', separable._cstack(cleft,cright))
print('separable._cstack(separable._separable(left), separable._separable(right)):\n', separable._cstack(separable._separable(left), separable._separable(right)))

args.summary: Investigated separability computation for nested CompoundModels. Found bug in astropy/modeling/separable.py in _cstack: when the right operand was an ndarray, the bottom-right block of the cright matrix was filled with scalar 1 instead of copying the ndarray values. This caused incorrect separability for nested compounds. Modified _cstack to copy the ndarray into the bottom-right block. Ran reproducibility checks: constructed the models from the PR description and compared separability matrices for nested and non-nested cases (they now match). Ran the separable test module; all tests passed locally. Committed the change.
